title: My Child Won’t Go to School… What’s Really Going On? (EBSNA Explained)

sentences.en: What if your professional expertise could earn you money even when you're not working?
sentences.zh: 如果你的专业知识即使在你没工作时也能为你赚钱，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and since 2019 I've been building additional income streams
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在建立额外的收入来源，

sentences.en: through books, online courses and memberships, and it's made such a difference to my business and my life.
sentences.zh: 通过书籍、在线课程和会员制，这给我的事业和生活带来了巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Tonight at 7pm, Sophie Foote is hosting a free Make Money Online Masterclass, exploring how you can turn your existing skills and knowledge into additional income streaMs.
sentences.zh: 今晚 7 点，Sophie Foote 将举办一场免费的“在线赚钱大师班”，探讨如何将你现有的技能和知识转化为额外的收入来源。

sentences.en: And I'd love more psychologists and mental health professionals to join us.
sentences.zh: 我非常希望更多的心理学家和心理健康专业人士能加入我们。

sentences.en: I'll be there too, supporting a lovely community of fellow psychologists, exploring what's possible beyond one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我也会参加，支持一个由心理学家同行组成的可爱社区，探索一对一工作之外的可能性。

sentences.en: Replays are available if you can't join live.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法参加直播，可以观看回放。

sentences.en: Click the link with this pre-roll or reach out to me on socials to grab your free place, because you can serve others and deserve financial freedom too.
sentences.zh: 点击此预告片旁边的链接，或在社交媒体上联系我以获取免费名额，因为你既可以服务他人，也理应获得财务自由。

sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about the phrase school refusal, because if I'm honest, it's one of those terms that never quite sits right with me.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考“拒绝上学”这个词，因为老实说，这个词让我感觉不太舒服。

sentences.en: Because when we say a child is refusing school, it sounds like willful defiance, like something intentional.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们说一个孩子拒绝上学时，听起来像是任性的反抗，像是蓄意为之。

sentences.en: But in my experience as a clinical psychologist, that's very rarely the case.
sentences.zh: 但在我作为临床心理学家的经验中，事实很少如此。

sentences.en: In this episode, I'm delighted to be rejoined by Dr. Adam McCartney, a qualified educational and child psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我很高兴能再次邀请到合格的教育与儿童心理学家 Adam McCartney 博士。

sentences.en: And together, we're thinking about what's often called emotional-based school avoidance,
sentences.zh: 我们将一起探讨通常所说的“情绪性回避上学”，

sentences.en: EBSA or EBSNA.
sentences.zh: 即 EBSA 或 EBSNA。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating insight into children, schools and parents.
sentences.zh: 这是对儿童、学校和家长之间关系的一次深刻洞察。

sentences.en: And stay tuned to learn what the most common age is for school refusal.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听，了解拒绝上学最常见的年龄段。

sentences.en: The answer might just surprise you.
sentences.zh: 答案可能会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到《心理学实际上》（Psychology Actually）。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne Trent 博士。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to reintroduce you to the wonderful Dr. Adam McCartney, who is a qualified education and child and community psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴再次向大家介绍出色的 Adam McCartney 博士，他是一位合格的教育、儿童与社区心理学家。

sentences.en: Hello again, Adam.
sentences.zh: 你好，Adam。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: It's great to be back with you, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能再次和你一起录节目，Marianne。

sentences.en: So nice to have you be back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来。

sentences.en: And we've been speaking about, actually, it'd be really helpful to think about an episode for what's called
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论，其实思考一期关于所谓的

sentences.en: Emotional-Based School Avoidance, sometimes called EBSA.
sentences.zh: “情绪性回避上学”（有时称为 EBSA）的节目会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: This seems to be something that really is a very emerging and pressing issue for so many schools and children and young people right now.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是目前许多学校、儿童和年轻人面临的一个非常新兴且紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what is EBSA?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们什么是 EBSA 吗？

sentences.en: It's essentially where children feel they are unable to attend school simply due to the level of stress, anxiety, or emotional demand
sentences.zh: 本质上，这是指孩子仅仅因为在进入教育环境时感受到的压力、焦虑或情感需求水平，

sentences.en: they feel from entering the education environment.
sentences.zh: 而感到自己无法上学。

sentences.en: I should stress as well, there's also another term, it's very similar but slightly nuanced, different, EBSNA.
sentences.zh: 我还应该强调，还有一个术语，非常相似但略有细微差别，即 EBSNA。

sentences.en: And the NA stands for non-attendance.
sentences.zh: NA 代表“非出勤”（non-attendance）。

sentences.en: And the reason that exists is the complexity of this topic is often met with judgment in one direction or the other.
sentences.zh: 之所以存在这个术语，是因为这个话题的复杂性往往会招致各方的评判。

sentences.en: And NA is trying to say that we're not looking at the child as being judged.
sentences.zh: 而使用 NA 是为了表明我们并不是在评判孩子。

sentences.en: So I think your viewers will appreciate that there's professionals out there who are always trying to remove the judgment factor on young people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你的观众会赞赏那些始终致力于消除对年轻人评判因素的专业人士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank you for introducing me to the term EBSNA because I wasn't aware of that and I will start to refer to it as that in future
sentences.zh: 感谢你向我介绍 EBSNA 这个术语，我之前并不知道，以后我会开始这样称呼它，

sentences.en: because I think language matters, but also, you know, this child and young person, they're already having a really hard time, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我认为语言很重要，而且，你知道，这些孩子和年轻人已经过得很艰难了，对吧？

sentences.en: And so how we're talking about this issue, both internally as a school, as a parent, as an education provider, but also to the child, that really matters, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以我们如何谈论这个问题——无论是作为学校内部、家长、教育提供者，还是对孩子而言——这真的很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Children, especially those in secondary school, are very attuned to feelings of judgment, feelings of shame, regardless of their developmental journey.
sentences.zh: 孩子们，尤其是中学生，对评判感和羞耻感非常敏感，无论他们处于什么样的成长阶段。

sentences.en: It's part of growing up.
sentences.zh: 这是成长的一部分。

sentences.en: Our teenage years are so heavily ingrained with forming our identities and how we relate to the education system is a huge part of that identity formation.
sentences.zh: 我们的青少年时期深深植根于身份的形成，而我们如何与教育系统建立联系，是这种身份形成的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And in the last 10 to 15 years, it has taken a drastic turn and we are seeing increasing numbers of EBSNA on EBSA,
sentences.zh: 在过去的 10 到 15 年里，情况发生了剧烈转变，我们看到 EBSNA 或 EBSA 的数量在增加，

sentences.en: but we're also seeing generally just students not being fulfilled by education anymore or not seeing the purpose of it in the same way that you or I might have seen in our days.
sentences.zh: 但我们也看到，学生们普遍不再从教育中获得满足感，或者不像你我当年那样看待教育的目的。

sentences.en: You know, I remember my own educational journey.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得我自己的求学经历。

sentences.en: The idea of not sitting in my GCSEs was like, it just was unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 不参加 GCSE 考试的想法简直是不可想象的。

sentences.en: But now students and young people are much more aware of opportunities, particularly online, about how to make money that isn't necessarily linked to a sound and quality education.
sentences.zh: 但现在学生和年轻人对机会的了解要多得多，尤其是在网上，关于如何赚钱，而不一定与扎实优质的教育挂钩。

sentences.en: So we need to do rethink this issue about what sort of demands we're placing on the young people today.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要重新思考这个问题，即我们今天对年轻人提出了什么样的要求。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm a big fan of Makita Oliver's podcast with Lily Allen.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是 Makita Oliver 和 Lily Allen 播客的忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: I'm taking a while to actually listen to the old episodes, so I'm still in the Lily era.
sentences.zh: 我花了一段时间才去听旧的剧集，所以我还停留在 Lily 的时代。

sentences.en: And it's actually quite rare that neither one of them say that they've got really a GCSE between them and they're in their early 40s.
sentences.zh: 其实很少见的是，她们两人都说自己几乎没什么 GCSE 证书，而她们都已经 40 多岁了。

sentences.en: But like you said, that isn't super common for someone who's kind of in their 40s because attendance was so kind of regimented
sentences.zh: 但就像你说的，对于 40 多岁的人来说，这并不常见，因为当时的考勤非常严格，

sentences.en: and getting yourself to these exams, like come hell or high water, like you are going.
sentences.zh: 而且无论发生什么，你都得去参加这些考试。

sentences.en: And it isn't so uncommon these days, I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意，这在今天确实不那么罕见了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, previously the two most important skill sets were literacy and numeracy.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，以前最重要的两项技能是读写能力和算术能力。

sentences.en: But now we've got technologically literate skills and children can learn them passively or they can learn them actively, but they don't always need the education system to do that.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们有了技术素养，孩子们可以被动或主动地学习这些技能，但他们并不总是需要教育系统来做到这一点。

sentences.en: How many young people have we seen learn coding on their own?
sentences.zh: 我们见过多少年轻人自学编程？

sentences.en: You know, I can't count the number of assessments I've done.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我数不清我做过多少次评估了。

sentences.en: It's like, well, you can't string a sentence together, but it can code.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，他连句子都写不通顺，但他会编程。

sentences.en: You know, these types of skills, it's a different world these young people live in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些类型的技能，这些年轻人生活在一个不同的世界里。

sentences.en: And what's vital for us as not only adults, but professionals working with them, is that we've got to appreciate that their value systems
sentences.zh: 作为成年人，更是作为与他们一起工作的专业人士，至关重要的是我们要意识到他们的价值体系

sentences.en: and their priorities are going to be different to what we experienced.
sentences.zh: 和优先事项将与我们所经历的不同。

sentences.en: It's very difficult then as a parent who's potentially, you know, getting letters saying your child's attendance is below the levels of expectation.
sentences.zh: 那么，作为一名家长，如果收到信件说你孩子的出勤率低于预期水平，这会非常困难。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think, am I right in saying that parents can be fined for that and can even face prosecution when actually if you, you know, firmly believe
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我说得对吗？家长可能会因此被罚款，甚至面临起诉，而实际上，如果你坚定地认为

sentences.en: that the education system is not a great fit for your child and yet you don't have the capacity to be able to home educate them yourselves,
sentences.zh: 教育系统并不适合你的孩子，但你又没有能力自己在家教育他们，

sentences.en: you really must be feeling in a, you know, caught between a rock and a hard place.
sentences.zh: 你一定感到进退两难。

sentences.en: You really must be.
sentences.zh: 你一定是的。

sentences.en: And I think the threshold for schools to start being worried about a child's attendance is something like 93% if it drops below that.
sentences.zh: 我认为学校开始担心孩子出勤率的门槛大约是 93%，如果低于这个水平的话。

sentences.en: It used to be as low as 82%, but I think the benchmarks have changed.
sentences.zh: 过去门槛低至 82%，但我认为基准已经改变了。

sentences.en: And what has happened with the punitive side, you know, you just mentioned parents being fined, different local authorities and different schools take a different approach to that.
sentences.zh: 关于惩罚方面，你刚才提到家长被罚款，不同的地方当局和不同的学校采取的方法不同。

sentences.en: Some go very much down that route and parents, you know, equally will push back on that through whatever legal channels they have.
sentences.zh: 有些学校非常倾向于走那条路，而家长们也会通过他们拥有的任何法律渠道进行反击。

sentences.en: And, but what that does is it causes distrust between the families and the schools and the legal frameworks cannot be punitive.
sentences.zh: 但这样做会导致家庭和学校之间的不信任，法律框架不能是惩罚性的。

sentences.en: They must be relational.
sentences.zh: 它们必须是基于关系的。

sentences.en: They must be community-based.
sentences.zh: 它们必须是基于社区的。

sentences.en: And because one, those parents will just leave that school and move on somewhere else until they can get that relationship.
sentences.zh: 因为第一，那些家长会直接离开那所学校，转到别处，直到他们能建立起那种关系。

sentences.en: But being that draconian approach to school just does, it's not conducive to long-term investment in young people.
sentences.zh: 但那种对学校采取严厉的方法，并不利于对年轻人进行长期投资。

sentences.en: They build up negative associations
sentences.zh: 他们会建立起负面联想，

sentences.en: and they just start to resent the system generally.
sentences.zh: 并开始普遍怨恨这个系统。

sentences.en: And it's avoidable.
sentences.zh: 这是可以避免的。

sentences.en: And we've got to work with the children.
sentences.zh: 我们必须与孩子们合作。

sentences.en: And, you know, all the cases I've worked with in terms of EBSNA, when the child is on the verge of not attending school,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我处理过的所有关于 EBSNA 的案例中，当孩子处于不上学的边缘时，

sentences.en: let's say they've got, still got in the 70% attendance rate, you can actually salvage that.
sentences.zh: 假设他们的出勤率还在 70% 左右，你实际上是可以挽救的。

sentences.en: The second they're at home full-time, the work that has to go in is exponentially higher.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们全职在家，所需要投入的工作量就会呈指数级增加。

sentences.en: It's not cost-effective at all.
sentences.zh: 这根本不划算。

sentences.en: And the gains are marginal.
sentences.zh: 而且收益微乎其微。

sentences.en: You know, it took me, I remember one case, it took me like two years to get them back into the school for one day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得有一个案例，我花了大约两年时间才让他们回学校待了一天。

sentences.en: And then sadly, they transitioned to secondary school and they were back to where they were.
sentences.zh: 然后可悲的是，他们升入中学后，又回到了原来的状态。

sentences.en: They stopped coming in again.
sentences.zh: 他们又停止上学了。

sentences.en: It just shows you the sensitivity of these cases.
sentences.zh: 这正好说明了这些案例的敏感性。

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I remember it well from CAMS, actually.
sentences.zh: 我从 CAMS（儿童与青少年心理健康服务）那里也记得很清楚。

sentences.en: At a certain point, in days gone by, there would be an automatic referral to CAMS at a certain level of threshold of attendance.
sentences.zh: 在过去，当出勤率达到一定门槛时，会自动转介到 CAMS。

sentences.en: I have to confess, I'm not sure if that still happens because maybe attendance is impacted upon more globally currently.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我不确定现在是否还会这样，因为也许目前出勤率受到更广泛的影响。

sentences.en: But then having to really work with the child, the young person and the teachers to kind of put in place a bespoke system really
sentences.zh: 但随后必须真正与孩子、年轻人和老师合作，建立一个定制的系统，

sentences.en: to optimally support this child or young person's attendance.
sentences.zh: 以最佳方式支持这个孩子或年轻人的出勤。

sentences.en: Not easy at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不容易。

sentences.en: No, and I feel like I'm the bearer of bad news at all times in this conversation because it doesn't look like it's going to get any better in the short term.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得我在这次谈话中一直是个坏消息的传递者，因为短期内情况似乎不会好转。

sentences.en: You know, for those who follow school or education-based news, every day there's another academy saying they're going to have to make redundancies due to budget cuts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于那些关注学校或教育新闻的人来说，每天都有另一所学院说由于预算削减，他们将不得不裁员。

sentences.en: And that's the world over the resources available to schools is diminishing.
sentences.zh: 全世界都是如此，学校可用的资源正在减少。

sentences.en: I know that the current government is talking about changing that and I hope to God they can.
sentences.zh: 我知道现任政府正在谈论改变这一点，我祈祷他们能做到。

sentences.en: But it is diminishing, which means that the teachers are expected to do more holding.
sentences.zh: 但资源确实在减少，这意味着老师们被期望承担更多的支持工作。

sentences.en: The TAs or the teaching assistants are expected to do more pastoral reactive work.
sentences.zh: 助教们被期望做更多的教牧反应工作。

sentences.en: And everybody essentially is expected to do more with less.
sentences.zh: 本质上，每个人都被期望用更少的资源做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And when you've got someone who's got a complex or sensitive emotional need that requires patience, being, holding for, you know, just for long periods of time,
sentences.zh: 当你面对一个有复杂或敏感情感需求的人，需要耐心、长时间的陪伴时，

sentences.en: and then the adult expected to do that has a high cognitive load, is under pressure from standards and practices, has got their head teacher asking to do six or seven
sentences.zh: 而那个被期望这样做的成年人本身认知负荷很高，承受着标准和实践的压力，校长还要求他们承担六七种

sentences.en: different roles.
sentences.zh: 不同的角色。

sentences.en: It's not really ideal situation, is it?
sentences.zh: 这真的不是理想的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: No, it really isn't.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不是。

sentences.en: It really isn't.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: And I was talking to my youngest child over dinner yesterday
sentences.zh: 昨天吃晚饭时，我正在和我的小儿子聊天，

sentences.en: and he was saying, oh, it'd be great if I didn't have to go to school because I could just be here all the time.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，如果我不必去上学就好了，因为我可以一直待在这里。

sentences.en: And I actually said to him,
sentences.zh: 我实际上对他说，

sentences.en: I kind of like the break when you're at school, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，当你去上学时，我挺喜欢那段休息时间的。

sentences.en: I love being your mum, but I don't like having to constantly think, is he okay?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做你的妈妈，但我不喜欢一直担心：他还好吗？

sentences.en: You know, and he has migraines and so we have to keep him hydrated like all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他有偏头痛，所以我们必须一直让他保持水分。

sentences.en: And so actually his attendance is not amazing because he gets these migraines.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上他的出勤率并不理想，因为他会偏头痛。

sentences.en: And I was like, I enjoy not having you there.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，我很享受你不在家的时候。

sentences.en: And actually, as I connect to that idea now, if I'm trying to operate a clinic or do my work from home when they're here,
sentences.zh: 实际上，当我联系到这个想法时，如果我试图在他们在家时经营诊所或在家工作，

sentences.en: I'm just biologically different.
sentences.zh: 我的生理状态确实不同。

sentences.en: I'm at a slightly more like less relaxed state and they're on my mind and it is hard.
sentences.zh: 我处于一种稍微不那么放松的状态，他们在我脑海里，这确实很难。

sentences.en: So I think any parent who has a child who's kind of struggling to get to school has got that mental load of having their child there
sentences.zh: 所以我认为任何有孩子难以去上学的家长，都有那种孩子在身边的心理负担，

sentences.en: when actually they may not really want them there, but they're allowing them to be there for their own child's wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们可能并不真的想让孩子待在家里，但他们为了孩子的福祉而允许他们待在家里。

sentences.en: But then it impacts on their ability to get their work or their tasks or just a little bit of quiet time where they can support their own wellbeing is so important.
sentences.zh: 但这会影响他们完成工作或任务的能力，或者仅仅是获得一点点可以支持自己福祉的安静时间，这非常重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is so important.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常重要。

sentences.en: I always say that teachers are the third parent and they are essentially, not only are they offering that respite care that you're talking about,
sentences.zh: 我总是说老师是第三位家长，他们本质上不仅提供了你所说的这种喘息式护理，

sentences.en: but they are taking that emotional load that a parent is expected to give
sentences.zh: 而且他们承担了家长被期望给予的情感负担，

sentences.en: and they are meeting that child in a nurturing, boundaried way so that they can support the social development into a fully functioning adult who is happy.
sentences.zh: 并以一种培育性的、有界限的方式去接触孩子，从而支持他们的社会化发展，使他们成为一个快乐、功能健全的成年人。

sentences.en: That's the ideal in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是理想状态。

sentences.en: And the important thing we've got to remember as parents is that in the modern day,
sentences.zh: 作为家长，我们必须记住重要的一点是，在现代，

sentences.en: I forgive you for believing that you're expected to do everything, but that's not realistic.
sentences.zh: 我原谅你认为自己被期望做所有事情，但这不现实。

sentences.en: And it's not how it used to be.
sentences.zh: 而且过去也不是这样的。

sentences.en: Child rearing was always community-based.
sentences.zh: 育儿总是基于社区的。

sentences.en: You always had people around you.
sentences.zh: 你身边总是有其他人。

sentences.en: You know, I remember talking to mothers and they always said, the first thing that comes up for a new mother is look after the mother.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得和母亲们交谈，她们总是说，新妈妈首先要考虑的是照顾好母亲。

sentences.en: They don't say look after the father.
sentences.zh: 她们不说照顾好父亲。

sentences.en: They do now in terms of pop culture, but they used to be look after the mother because the sanity of the parents
sentences.zh: 现在流行文化中会提，但过去通常是照顾好母亲，因为家长的理智

sentences.en: automatically supports the sanity of the child.
sentences.zh: 会自动支持孩子的理智。

sentences.en: But if you've got a high demand environment and low resources, whether it's in your home or at school, everybody suffers.
sentences.zh: 但如果你处于一个高需求、低资源的环境中，无论是在家里还是在学校，每个人都会受苦。

sentences.en: Everybody then places it within child because it's the loudest voice, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会把问题归咎于孩子，因为孩子的声音最大，可以这么说。

sentences.en: But everybody's resilience is low.
sentences.zh: 但每个人的韧性都很低。

sentences.en: Child, teachers, parents.
sentences.zh: 孩子、老师、家长。

sentences.en: Essentially, we've got to move back to a community-based way of approaching education, approaching home life, and getting out of the silo and martyrdom type stuff that we've done.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我们必须回到一种基于社区的方式来处理教育、处理家庭生活，摆脱我们过去那种孤立和自我牺牲的模式。

sentences.en: I wrote a post about a year ago around education's built on goodwill.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，我写了一篇关于教育建立在善意之上的文章。

sentences.en: It's built on the fact that teachers will take that extra 20 minutes after school to do some admin or they will mark their books at home.
sentences.zh: 它建立在老师们愿意在放学后多花 20 分钟处理行政工作，或者在家里批改作业的事实之上。

sentences.en: Really, that needs to be built into the school day.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这需要被纳入学校的一天中。

sentences.en: We look at the, in Finland, the Finnish system, the teacher delivers the main core aspects of the curriculum and then spends the afternoon planning every single day.
sentences.zh: 我们看看芬兰的系统，老师负责课程的核心部分，然后每天下午花时间备课。

sentences.en: And they have a team around them who are competent in delivering their plans.
sentences.zh: 他们身边有一个团队，有能力执行他们的计划。

sentences.en: And some schools might say they do this, but from what I understand, it's a very robust system over there.
sentences.zh: 有些学校可能会说他们也这样做，但据我了解，那里的系统非常稳健。

sentences.en: Very interesting.
sentences.zh: 非常有意思。

sentences.en: Before we continue, it's time for a quick behind-the-therapy-room-door moment brought to you by WriteUp, who are the practice management system I use in my own clinical practice.
sentences.zh: 在继续之前，先来一段“治疗室门后”的简短时刻，本环节由 WriteUp 赞助，这也是我在自己的临床实践中使用的诊所管理系统。

sentences.en: One thing that often comes up in trauma and addiction work is how important it is for people to feel safe enough to tell their story at their own pace.
sentences.zh: 在创伤和成瘾治疗中，人们经常提到的一点是，让来访者感到足够安全，从而能按照自己的节奏讲述自己的故事，这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: In therapy, the details of someone's experiences can emerge slowly over time, sometimes across many sessions.
sentences.zh: 在治疗过程中，来访者的经历细节可能会随着时间慢慢浮现，有时甚至需要跨越多次会谈。

sentences.en: But for that work to happen, people actually need to be able to get to their sessions.
sentences.zh: 但要实现这些工作，人们首先得能来参加会谈。

sentences.en: And when someone is at a vulnerable stage in their recovery, small things like clear appointment reminders, easy communication, and reliable scheduling can make a real difference
sentences.zh: 当一个人处于康复的脆弱阶段时，一些小事，比如清晰的预约提醒、便捷的沟通以及可靠的日程安排，真的能起到很大作用，

sentences.en: in helping them stay connected to the work.
sentences.zh: 帮助他们保持与治疗工作的联系。

sentences.en: WriteUp is trusted by over 50,000 clinicians.
sentences.zh: WriteUp 深受超过 50,000 名临床医生的信赖。

sentences.en: If you'd like to try it yourself, you can access a free trial for up to five users using the link in the description and the code MARIANN30.
sentences.zh: 如果您想亲自尝试，可以使用描述中的链接并输入代码 MARIANN30，即可获得最多支持五名用户的免费试用。

sentences.en: Now back to the show.
sentences.zh: 现在回到节目。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what the most common age tends to be for children or young people starting to experience more signs of emotional-based school non-attendance?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们，儿童或青少年开始出现更多“情绪性拒绝上学”（EBSNA）迹象的常见年龄段通常是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: We naturally think that it would be GCSEs because that is the test time.
sentences.zh: 我们自然会认为是 GCSE（英国中考）阶段，因为那是考试的时候。

sentences.en: A lot of stress for a lot of students.
sentences.zh: 对很多学生来说压力很大。

sentences.en: But it's actually in Key Stage 3, and that's Year 7 through to Year 9.
sentences.zh: 但实际上是在关键阶段 3（Key Stage 3），也就是 7 年级到 9 年级。

sentences.en: We usually get a grace period in Year 7 of students being able to tolerate a new environment, getting a bit used to the transition, and then they make a decision emotionally
sentences.zh: 我们通常会在 7 年级给学生一个宽限期，让他们去适应新环境，习惯这种过渡，然后他们在情感上做出决定，

sentences.en: whether they like that transition or not.
sentences.zh: 决定他们是否喜欢这种过渡。

sentences.en: And usually by the end of Year 7, beginning of Year 8, we will start to see these rises.
sentences.zh: 通常到 7 年级结束、8 年级开始时，我们就会开始看到这些比例上升。

sentences.en: Interestingly, the EBSNA also matches trends in exclusion.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，EBSNA 的趋势也与停学（exclusion）的趋势相吻合。

sentences.en: So we know at Key Stage 3 exclusions rise rapidly, particularly in the last 14 years.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，在关键阶段 3，停学率迅速上升，特别是在过去 14 年里。

sentences.en: And we think that's got to do with the increase in academic demand, but also the moving from primary school to secondary school where behaviour systems are much more rigid
sentences.zh: 我们认为这与学术要求的提高有关，也与从小学升入中学有关，因为中学的行为准则要严格得多，

sentences.en: and expectations are much more in line with academic achievement.
sentences.zh: 而且对学生的要求也更侧重于学业成绩。

sentences.en: That makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 这非常有道理。

sentences.en: And actually having my own eldest child be currently in Year 8, you see them join Year 7 and have a lot of energy and enthusiasm and excitement for,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我自己的大孩子现在就在 8 年级，你看着他们刚进 7 年级时，充满了活力、热情和兴奋，

sentences.en: you know, I've got more than one classroom now and I've got all these teachers to kind of work with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会想：“我现在不止一个教室了，我有这么多老师要打交道。”

sentences.en: And then I saw it kind of dip off that enthusiasm and then it becomes real life.
sentences.zh: 然后我看着那种热情逐渐消退，生活变得现实起来。

sentences.en: And I wonder if it's something about not feeling as emotionally held as they did by their previous primary school teachers, which often is just one or two teachers.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑这是否与他们不再像在小学时那样感到在情感上被“接纳”有关，因为小学通常只有一两位老师。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And, you know, we just spoke about viewing your teacher as the third parent and it is having that relationship with at least one or two teachers at secondary school.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们刚才谈到把老师视为“第三位家长”，在中学里，至少与一两位老师建立这种关系确实很重要。

sentences.en: You move between classes, you may have five classes in a day.
sentences.zh: 你需要在不同教室间穿梭，一天可能有五节课。

sentences.en: My own school, I think we had up to eight different teachers in a day.
sentences.zh: 我自己的学校，我想我们一天最多有八位不同的老师。

sentences.en: And that can be a blessing and a curse, those many transitions.
sentences.zh: 这种频繁的转换既是福也是祸。

sentences.en: The thing is, if you don't like your teacher, you only have to suck them up for like 30 or 40 minutes.
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果你不喜欢某个老师，你只需要忍受他们 30 或 40 分钟。

sentences.en: I'm actually developing some training with a friend and colleague,
sentences.zh: 我实际上正在和一位朋友兼同事一起开发一些培训课程，

sentences.en: Matt Robson, who went through this in his journey, whereby he didn't have a great educational experience, but it was the relationship with his maths teacher
sentences.zh: 他叫马特·罗布森（Matt Robson），他经历过这些，他的教育经历并不美好，但正是与数学老师的关系，

sentences.en: that got him through it.
sentences.zh: 让他挺了过来。

sentences.en: And, you know, the story he told me was as he was leaving the classroom after a bad day, the maths teacher called him back and said, what are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他告诉我的故事是，在糟糕的一天结束后，他正要离开教室，数学老师把他叫住说：“我们要怎么做？”

sentences.en: How are we going to get you through this?
sentences.zh: “我们要怎么帮你度过难关？”

sentences.en: And what that does is one adult seeing the child and saying, I care about you.
sentences.zh: 这就是一位成年人看到了这个孩子，并说：“我在乎你。”

sentences.en: I'm going to do something for you.
sentences.zh: “我会为你做点什么。”

sentences.en: I'm going to get alongside you.
sentences.zh: “我会陪在你身边。”

sentences.en: And that's vital.
sentences.zh: 这至关重要。

sentences.en: That is absolutely vital.
sentences.zh: 这绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: I remember even doing A levels and I was quite naturally good at biology.
sentences.zh: 我记得我读 A-level 的时候，我天生就擅长生物。

sentences.en: It was my favorite subject.
sentences.zh: 那是我最喜欢的科目。

sentences.en: And my mock exams, I got a high B.
sentences.zh: 模拟考试时，我拿了个高分 B。

sentences.en: I was okay with that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得还可以。

sentences.en: My teacher just said, that's not good enough for you.
sentences.zh: 我的老师却说：“这对你来说还不够好。”

sentences.en: And what he was saying was, you're capable of more.
sentences.zh: 他想表达的是，你有能力做得更好。

sentences.en: And he just telling me, I believe in you.
sentences.zh: 他只是在告诉我，我相信你。

sentences.en: And it's that belief that spurred me on to go and study and really work hard at it.
sentences.zh: 正是这种信任激励我去学习，并为此付出了巨大的努力。

sentences.en: And it was because I liked him, he liked me, that then that dopamine I was telling you about.
sentences.zh: 而且是因为我喜欢他，他也喜欢我，才产生了那种我之前提到的多巴胺。

sentences.en: I was in the optimal level to pursue the learning journey a bit further.
sentences.zh: 我处于追求学习之旅的最佳状态。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: And it's the idea that we spoke about before about emotionally collecting the children, young people that you're working with if you're working in a school.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们之前谈到的，如果你在学校工作，要从情感上“接纳”你所教的孩子和年轻人。

sentences.en: And actually, that sounds like you were emotionally collected, you were held in mind, which then made you want to work really hard, not just for yourself, but for that relationship
sentences.zh: 事实上，听起来你当时就是被情感上接纳了，你被老师放在心上，这让你不仅为了自己，也为了那段对你来说非常重要的关系，

sentences.en: that was really important to you.
sentences.zh: 而想要努力学习。

sentences.en: And that is a really important consideration, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的考量。

sentences.en: Absolutely, it is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I'm aware that locally there are kind of education attendance buses that come and round the children up and drag them back into school.
sentences.zh: 我知道在当地有一些教育出勤巴士，会把孩子们围起来，强行带回学校。

sentences.en: And sometimes as a parent, you might think that's the only thing you can do is to kind of try and facilitate getting your child on this bus or bundling them yourself into the car
sentences.zh: 有时作为家长，你可能会觉得你能做的唯一一件事，就是设法让孩子上那辆车，或者亲自把他们塞进车里，

sentences.en: and getting them to school.
sentences.zh: 送他们去学校。

sentences.en: There's a whole lot of distress,
sentences.zh: 这其中充满了痛苦，

sentences.en: I think, for the child and the parent there.
sentences.zh: 我想，对孩子和家长来说都是如此。

sentences.en: Is there anything else that a parent can do if they're struggling with a child or young person who's got signs or symptoms of EBSNA?
sentences.zh: 如果家长正在为有 EBSNA 迹象或症状的孩子或年轻人而挣扎，他们还能做些什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, just hearing you talk about these buses, it's so distressing and upsetting.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，听到你谈论这些巴士，真的让人感到非常痛苦和沮丧。

sentences.en: And what's the most vital thing, again, it's coming back to community-based relationships.
sentences.zh: 最重要的事情，再次强调，还是要回归到基于社区的关系上。

sentences.en: when you are that parent, it is vital that you can form some sort of relationship with the school.
sentences.zh: 当你作为家长时，与学校建立某种关系至关重要。

sentences.en: Quite often, there'll be one person, a voice of contact, and it's, say, usually it's the Senko or pastoral lead.
sentences.zh: 通常会有一个人作为联络人，比如特殊教育需求协调员（SENCO）或教牧主管。

sentences.en: And they are really useful in terms of helping you understand what's going on inside the school, and that's a vital relationship to have.
sentences.zh: 他们在帮助你了解学校内部情况方面非常有用，建立这种关系至关重要。

sentences.en: But if I was a parent in that situation, I would be asking questions about which teacher does my child like?
sentences.zh: 但如果我是处于那种情况下的家长，我会问：我的孩子喜欢哪位老师？

sentences.en: And how can my child use that relationship to enjoy coming into school?
sentences.zh: 我的孩子如何利用这种关系来享受上学？

sentences.en: And when I work with schools, I often talk about what does their pastoral system look like?
sentences.zh: 当我和学校合作时，我经常谈论他们的教牧系统是什么样的？

sentences.en: And in my mind,
sentences.zh: 在我的脑海里，

sentences.en: I'm thinking about secondary schools.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是中学。

sentences.en: They tend to have their pastoral systems as, you know, there's rooms that they go into and they go and meet the pastoral lead and you'll talk to them.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于把教牧系统设为：你知道，就是学生去某个房间，见教牧主管，然后和他们交谈。

sentences.en: However, I feel like it needs to be more threaded throughout the school environment.
sentences.zh: 然而，我觉得它需要更深入地渗透到整个学校环境中。

sentences.en: I had a long discussion with actually a head teacher the other day and we both came to the conclusion that the core subject leads need to have pastoral training.
sentences.zh: 前几天我和一位校长进行了深入讨论，我们都得出结论：核心科目的负责人需要接受教牧培训。

sentences.en: That is your English and your maths because you spend the most time with your English and your maths teacher.
sentences.zh: 也就是英语和数学老师，因为你花在他们身上的时间最多。

sentences.en: So if you can have some sort of pastoral support coming from them every single day, that's drip feeding.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你每天都能从他们那里得到某种教牧支持，那就是一种“滴灌式”的关怀。

sentences.en: And we know little and often works better.
sentences.zh: 我们知道“少量多次”效果更好。

sentences.en: So again, going back to what parents can do, it's asking, does my child like the maths teacher?
sentences.zh: 所以，回到家长能做什么，就是要问：我的孩子喜欢数学老师吗？

sentences.en: Does my child like the English teacher?
sentences.zh: 我的孩子喜欢英语老师吗？

sentences.en: If not, how do we nurture that relationship?
sentences.zh: 如果没有，我们该如何培养这种关系？

sentences.en: And it's those types of conversations that are really vital.
sentences.zh: 这些类型的对话才是真正至关重要的。

sentences.en: They don't feel like you're going to be, you won't get a turnaround overnight and it's not some sort of discreet intervention like going in and doing some ELSA work,
sentences.zh: 它们不会让你觉得马上就能立竿见影，这也不是某种离散的干预措施，比如进去做一些 ELSA 工作，

sentences.en: emotional literacy work.
sentences.zh: 即情感素养工作。

sentences.en: this is much more, it's more nuanced but it's much more powerful.
sentences.zh: 这更微妙，但力量更强大。

sentences.en: Okay, so a really good question for a parent then of a prospective primary school student or a secondary school student, if they're going to an open evening, would be to check out
sentences.zh: 好的，那么对于准小学生或中学生的家长来说，如果他们去参加开放日，一个非常好的问题就是去了解，

sentences.en: and to ask, what is your pastoral care like?
sentences.zh: 并询问：你们的教牧关怀是怎样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, that is a really good question and have your follow-up questions, is it just a single team?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常好的问题，还要准备好后续问题：这只是一个单一的团队吗？

sentences.en: Is it just a couple of people?
sentences.zh: 只有几个人负责吗？

sentences.en: Or is there a relational policy throughout the entire school?
sentences.zh: 还是整个学校都有这种关系导向的政策？

sentences.en: If the school's really open and honest, they might share that relational policy with you.
sentences.zh: 如果学校非常开放和诚实，他们可能会与你分享这种关系政策。

sentences.en: What would a relational policy look like?
sentences.zh: 什么是关系政策？

sentences.en: Because I've never heard of that term before from a school setting.
sentences.zh: 因为我以前从未在学校环境中听说过这个词。

sentences.en: They're not super common.
sentences.zh: 它们并不常见。

sentences.en: When I was working in the LA, we had a huge project and it was fabulous.
sentences.zh: 当我在地方当局工作时，我们有一个巨大的项目，非常棒。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Where we would help schools set up their relational policies.
sentences.zh: 我们帮助学校建立他们的关系政策。

sentences.en: And it's essentially to remove the behavioural policy and reframe everything in a positive light rather than cause and consequences.
sentences.zh: 本质上是移除行为惩戒政策，以积极的视角重新构建一切，而不是基于因果和后果。

sentences.en: So for example, one school that I supported with was when a child was escalating through the challenging behaviour stuff rather than going down the punitive route.
sentences.zh: 例如，我支持的一所学校，当孩子在挑战性行为中升级时，他们没有走惩罚路线。

sentences.en: It was which adults then need to get alongside that.
sentences.zh: 而是考虑哪些成年人需要介入并陪伴在孩子身边。

sentences.en: So for example, in the first instance, it might be spending five extra minutes with their English teacher at lunchtime or something like that.
sentences.zh: 例如，最初可能是在午餐时间多花五分钟和英语老师待在一起之类的。

sentences.en: Then once it got to a certain threshold, each school will have a different set of needs.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦达到某个阈值，每所学校的需求不同。

sentences.en: So I don't want to be too specific.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想说得太具体。
